evals.prompt: /hand-and-brain we're moving the whole api package off moment.js onto date-fns. there are like 60 files that import moment across src/api and src/jobs, plus the tests. I don't want you burning your whole context on this. You're running as Opus in Claude Code.
evals.expected_output: Opus stays the orchestrator: announces the roster, has a cheap hand inventory the usages, decides the migration rules itself, fans mechanical edits out to cheaper same-family hands on disjoint files, and verifies before reporting.
expectations: States a one-line roster naming the brain model and the hand model(s) before starting work
Delegates the usage inventory or search to a subagent rather than reading the ~60 files inline
Every subagent call sets an explicit model that is a lower tier in the same family (Sonnet or Haiku), not the session default
Uses the fast tier (Haiku) for search or inventory and the capable tier (Sonnet) for the code edits, or justifies a different split
The brain itself decides the moment-to-date-fns mapping rules and puts them in the briefs, instead of telling hands to work out the approach
Parallel editing hands are given disjoint sets of files
Each brief states what done looks like (or the exact question to answer) and a return shape with a length cap and no file dumps
Verifies the hands' work itself (runs tests or reads diffs) before telling the user it is done, and distinguishes verified results from hand claims

Gives the reason in terms of delegation overhead versus a known-target edit

expectations: Uses the GPT Luna model as the hand because the user named it, rather than defaulting to Sonnet or Haiku

Reaches Luna through a headless CLI call with an explicit model flag or through an orchestrator's cross-provider delegation, using an exact model id resolved from a model list or config rather than the bare nickname
